modelF_scan.eigenvalue_audit: eigenvalues of S are exactly (-sigma0, 0, P0, P0) for all v (see modelF_eigenvalue_check): the EC verdict of the rotating fluid is the STATIC verdict for every (q, A, v). DEC needs sigma0 >= |P0| with sigma0 < 0: impossible. 0 pass rows.

modelF_threshold.threshold_law: sigma_stat(v=0.5) >= 0 iff A >= 7 (analytic: (gamma^2-1)(A-1)/2 >= 1 with gamma^2-1 = 1/3 at v=0.5)

modelG.law: (sigma, P) -> lambda (sigma0, P0), lambda = sqrt(1 + alpha^2/(a^2 (1-q))) >= 1: every margin keeps its sign, |sigma| and |P| grow. No statically failing row can flip.

part_a.O_Omega_theorem: CONFIRMED (analytic): sigma, P even in Omega (time-reversal / Hartle structure: O(Omega) is g_tphi frame dragging only, plus the S^t_phi Lanczos component). Any sigma shift is O(Omega^2).
part_a.not_computable: Full second-order Hartle junction (h0/m0/h2/m2 with shell source + cross terms): no Hartle solver exists in the programme record; all engines on hand are static-spherical or FD judges requiring an explicit metric. Models F (matter side, exact) and G (geometry side, equatorial reduction) bound the two channels the Hartle solve would mix; both fail independently (eigenvalue invariance; lambda >= 1).
part_a.deciding_terms: Model F: Hawking-Ellis eigenvalues of the rotating surface fluid are rotation-invariant (-sigma0, P0, P0) with sigma0 = -sqrt(1-q)/(2 pi a) < 0 — DEC/WEC fail at every v <= 0.5. Model G: equatorial Kerr jump rescales (sigma, P) by lambda >= 1 — required sigma becomes MORE negative.

beta_star_scaling.argument: LABELLED SCALING ARGUMENT: (1) by part (a), rotating the wall matter does not change its Hawking-Ellis eigenvalues — rotation is not an SEC supply channel for existing matter; (2) frame-dragging corrections to the REQUIRED tensor enter at O((Omega a)^2) <= 0.25 times the local wall stress scale, with sign fixed by the geometry (centrifugal, i.e. it unloads the wall isotropically, not preferentially on the binding SEC combination at the inner edge); (3) priced with the numbers above: even crediting ALL of u_rot,max = (1/2) rho_wall v^2 at v = 0.5 as SEC supply at the binding site, it reaches only ~0.27x the beta=0.0275 deficit (2.5e-5) and ~0.03x the beta=0.1 deficit scale (~2e-4, Phase 17/Phase 6 records). Rotation does not lift the ceiling out of the bracket (0.025, 0.0275]; it is short by ~4x at the first illegal point before any sign/structure discount.

part_b.verdict_clause: DEC at M_bg=4 fails at every a* <= 0.9 in both reduction variants on the shell own (difference) tensor — the H4/AdS-convention judge for a background carrying its own tensor — at -5.4e-5 to -6.8e-5, and the difference-tensor DEC crossing stays at M_bg = 2.54-2.60 (control: 2.55): spin does NOT move the shell crossing. The one apparent exception — core TOTAL tensor at (averaged, a*=0.6, M_bg=4): DEC +8.98e-6, all core ECs > 0 — does not meet the bar: (i) it is a core-only cancellation against the spherical reduction effective background fields, which are themselves EC-illegal at the inner edge (bg core NEC -6.7e-5 averaged a*=0.6; -4.1e-4 equatorial a*=0.9) and have NO counterpart in true Kerr (vacuum); (ii) the same row fails on the full band (band total NEC -3.1e-4), where the shell tapers off and the background illegality stands alone. Total-tensor crossings (2.86-3.81) are therefore reduction artefacts, reported for the record. Genuine axisymmetric Kerr re-solve: NOT COMPUTABLE with the programme machinery (no axisymmetric shell solver; the FD judge audits metrics but cannot construct the re-equilibrated shell in one) — named reopening condition, not the verdict basis: the sanctioned equatorial/averaged reduction was computable and fails. beta* ceiling: scaling argument (above) — rotation short by ~4x at beta=0.0275, ceiling unmoved.
